issue: User wrote a greeting ('Kris, pryvit') and the bot accused them of copying/pasting text
root_cause: _enhance_prompt was applied to ALL messages without exception; Haiku rewrote the phatic greeting into template-looking text, the main Claude received that enhanced version instead of the original and (fairly, from its view) accused the user of copying — the text WAS generated, but by Haiku, not the user
solution: Added an instruction to the _enhance_prompt system prompt: if the phrase is phatic communication (greeting, farewell, thanks, short reaction) — return it unchanged; do not 'improve' what is not a query
preventive_measure: Intermediate LLM transformations can distort user intent; not every message is a 'query' to enhance — phatic communication is a social signal, not an informational one

issue: Kris's photo-reply text appeared truncated (~80 chars, cut mid-word) in the Telegram log group, while the recipient received the full message
root_cause: MSG_OUT log emit in the photo handler sliced the reply to 80 chars (f"{BOT_NAME}: {response[:80]}" at bot.py:259) — a legacy pattern from BOT_TEMPLATE in ai-office-shared/agents/coder.py; the delivery path (send_long) was never truncated, so only the log copy was cut
solution: Removed the [:80] slice so MSG_OUT logs the full reply, matching the text and HTTP handlers; the same fix applied fleet-wide (villy-bot, prophet-bot, pilly-bot-bot, railway-deployer-bot) and to BOT_TEMPLATE itself; logger-bot's central MAX_MSG_LEN=3800 guard with the explicit '… [обрезано]' marker remains the single truncation point
preventive_measure: Log emitters must not pre-truncate — length limiting is owned solely by logger-bot; BOT_TEMPLATE no longer stamps [:80] into newly generated bots

issue: Kris rejected two genuine requests from Yana as 'a question the system asked itself' / 'text that was not meant for me', and stayed silent on images sent as files. Group messages from other bots crashed instead of being answered.
root_cause: Three independent defects. (1) process() at bot.py:287 did `message = await enhance_prompt(message, claude_async)` — Haiku's rewrite REPLACED the user's text, so the main model never saw Yana's Ukrainian words and reacted to a translated/meta artifact; the substitution was logged nowhere while MSG_IN still showed the original. (2) handle_photo was registered on filters.PHOTO only and returned bare on group chats, so an image sent as a document was matched by no handler at all and a group image was dropped without a word. (3) `random` was never imported although handle_group_bot_message used random.random(), so that handler raised NameError on every group message; `weekly_review` was likewise called but not imported, breaking the /cron/weekly_review endpoint.
solution: process() now uses enhance_prompt_ex: the ORIGINAL text goes into history and the validated enhancement, if any, is appended to the SYSTEM prompt via intent_hint() and marked as machine-generated. handle_photo uses shared.media.extract_image (photo + Document.IMAGE, real media_type, size/mime validation) and replies with ImageError.user_message instead of returning silently; in groups it answers when addressed_in_group() matches. Registered IMAGE_FILTER instead of filters.PHOTO. The dead analyze_photo function and its unreachable call (which referenced an undefined SYSTEM_PROMPT) were deleted. Added the missing `random` and `weekly_review` imports. The feature-request path now calls shared.dev_escalation.request_dev_feature, writing a real dev-dept task to the taskboard instead of a DM to a hardcoded chat id. All background asyncio.create_task calls replaced with shared.tasks.spawn.
preventive_measure: Run pyflakes, not just py_compile, before shipping a bot — py_compile does not catch undefined names and both crashes here had been live in production. Never let an intermediate LLM own the authoritative user input. A handler that returns without replying is a bug: every rejection path needs a user-visible message.
